messages:
maria: Quick flag — sampleapp stress test shows massive burst when paginated endpoint retries 429s + token refresh. Dev-dedicated GPU pool gets saturated in <30s. Logs: ```ERROR 429 rate_limit exceeded; retrying page=5```

sam: Ugh. Is that using the JS SDK default retry + concurrency? We recently turned on auto-retry in sampleapp.

leo: FWIW the Go client uses a token-bucket limiter per-route, JS uses windowed concurrency + exponential backoff. They behave very differently under pagination loops.

ana: Repro steps? I can flip a flag locally. Also can set `maxInflightRequests` to 8 and `retryOn429: false` in the short term.

maria: Repro is easy: run samples/paginate-bulk with `--parallel-pages=20` against devdedicated. It'll spawn 20 concurrent page fetches which then all retry when upstream returns 429.

tamir: Proposed fix: SDK should honor server-provided rate headers and apply per-route in-flight caps. Also add a jittered adaptive backoff that scales with number of concurrent paginators in the process. RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/332

sam: I'll add an e2e that simulates 429 bursts + delayed token refresh to catch regressions. Also log X-RateLimit headers in sampleapp to help ops.

devex-bot: issue created (#4567) by sam: "js-sdk: consistent concurrency limiter + adaptive backoff for paginated endpoints" assigned to @sam, @tamir

maria: Should we change JS SDK default to `maxInflightRequests: 6` for paginated helpers until we ship parity changes?

leo: Agree. Also document the difference in the SDK migration guide — people hit this during onboarding. I'll write a short blurb.

ana: For release notes: call out sampleapp paywall where we changed defaults and add a short troubleshooting FAQ about "429 storms".

maria: Thanks — let's get the quick mitigation in sampleapp and an SDK patch for the next minor. :thumbsup:
